actions.name: list_books
actions.intent: Returns every book currently in the reading log. Use this to see the full collection, to find a book's id before calling get_book/update_book/delete_book, or to check whether a book already exists before creating a new entry.
actions.whenNotToUse: Do not use this to look up a single known book by id — use get_book instead, which is more direct and returns a not_found error you can act on if the id turns out to be wrong.

actions.name: get_book
actions.intent: Returns a single book's full details (title, author, review) by its id. Use this when you already know the book's id and need its current details.
actions.whenNotToUse: Do not use this to check whether a book already exists before creating one — book titles are not required to be unique in this log; use list_books and inspect the results instead.

id.description: The book's id, from list_books or a prior create_book/update_book result.

errors.description: No book exists with the given id.

actions.name: create_book
actions.intent: Adds a new book entry to the reading log with a title, author, and an optional review. Use this when the reader started or finished a book that is not yet in the log.
actions.whenNotToUse: Do not use this to change an existing book's details — use update_book with the book's id instead; create_book always makes a new, separate entry.

idempotencyKey.description: Caller-supplied opaque string. Reusing the same key with the same parameters replays the original result instead of creating a duplicate.

errors.description: idempotencyKey was already used for a call with different parameters.

actions.name: update_book
actions.intent: Replaces an existing book's title, author, and review with new values. Use this to correct a typo, add or change a review, or otherwise update a book already in the log.
actions.whenNotToUse: Do not use this to change a single field in isolation — this API has no partial patch, update_book always replaces bookName, author, and review together, so pass the full current values for any field you are not changing. Do not use it to try to undo a delete_book — deletion is irreversible, there is nothing left to update back.

idempotencyKey.description: Caller-supplied opaque string. Reusing the same key with the same parameters replays the original result.

errors.description: No book exists with the given id.
idempotencyKey was already used for a call with different parameters.

actions.name: delete_book
actions.intent: Permanently removes a book entry from the reading log. This is irreversible — there is no undo. Always call first with dryRun: true to preview the book being deleted and obtain a confirmationToken, then call again with that token to actually delete it.
actions.whenNotToUse: Do not call this for real (dryRun absent/false) without first previewing it — it will be rejected without a valid confirmationToken from a matching prior dry-run. If you want a backup before deleting, call export_books first, since the deletion cannot be undone afterward.

idempotencyKey.description: Caller-supplied opaque string, required on every call (preview and confirm).

dryRun.description: Set true to preview the delete and obtain a confirmationToken, without deleting anything.

confirmationToken.description: Token returned by a prior dry-run for this exact book. Required to actually delete.

outputSchema.description: On a real delete: { deleted: true, id }. On a dry-run: the guardrail preview shape (dryRun, preview, impact, confirmationToken).

errors.description: No book exists with the given id.
Real delete called without a valid, matching confirmationToken from a prior dry-run.
idempotencyKey was already used for a call with a different id.

actions.name: export_books
actions.intent: Writes every current book entry to a books.json file in the server's working directory, for backup or offline use. Use this when the reader wants their reading log exported or backed up to a file, or before calling delete_book if they may want the deleted entry back later.
actions.whenNotToUse: Do not use this to read the current book list back into the conversation — use list_books, which returns the data directly instead of writing it to a server-side file. A replay of the same idempotencyKey returns the originally-exported snapshot, not a fresh export — use a new idempotencyKey to force a fresh export.

idempotencyKey.description: Caller-supplied opaque string. Reusing the same key replays the original export result instead of writing again.

path.description: Path to the written JSON file, relative to the server's working directory.

errors.description: Writing the export file failed (disk I/O).
idempotencyKey was already used for a prior export call.
